No, I don't agree with it, for several reasons. Here are a few:

1) Although sometimes it seems justified, it is not fairly applied to all crimes of similar heinousness. It depends a lot on whether you can afford a good lawyer whether you get the death penalty. Many years ago I worked on a project to get clemency for a man sentenced to death. Let me hasten to add that there was no question that he killed two people and seriously wounded a third: and the shooting was witnessed by a six year old girl who was related to all three victims, one of which was the child's mother. The killer was 19 years old, and high as a kite on coke at the time. He took, he thought, a plea deal, but his public defender lawyer screwed it up and he wound up with the death penalty anyway. I met him after he'd been on death row for over a decade. He was a different person. He'd gotten off drugs, obviously, found God, and was extremely remorseful for what he'd done. (You can be cynical about that, but wouldn't you rather have him remorseful than otherwise?) He made an appeal based on ineffective assistance of counsel, but it failed, still, having seen what happened I'm sure if he'd had a skilled attorney he would have gotten life. I'm not just making it up: imposition of the death penalty in my state was so unfairly applied that a few years later it was abolished. (I should note, I was involved in this as a school project, not because going in I had a particular opposition to the death penalty. The experience really changed by view.)

2) The death penalty is very permanent. Every year we find out about another innocent person who was wrongly convicted. It's one thing to have an innocent person locked up for decades, at least they have their life and you can let them free. But if we execute them, that's all she wrote.

3) It doesn't seem very effective as a deterrent. (Note guy in my story under point #1. It didn't stop him from killing those people.)

4) Death row is really expensive, in terms of constant appeals. You can go the Texas way and execute people quickly, but then, they've executed some innocent folks. And condemned prisoners are harder to control, because what do they have to lose?
